title: eval-harness: add CI hook for prompt-set regression gating and metric export
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: CI currently runs end-to-end evals but we lack a lightweight gating hook that will fail PRs when prompt-set regressions (measured by configured metrics and thresholds) are detected. This PR adds a new eval-harness CI hook (redwood-eval-gate) which: 1) runs a targeted subset of prompt-sets (fast path) during PR checks, 2) computes configured metrics (EM, F1, BLEU, avg logprob) and compares them against baseline thresholds, 3) exports metric deltas to our metrics backend and annotates the PR with short summaries, and 4) provides a diagnostic artifact bundle (failed prompts + model outputs + diff) for quick triage. Changes: implemented a new CLI entrypoint (redwood_eval_gate) that can be invoked from CI with --profile and --thresholds; added lightweight YAML profiles under eval-harness/profiles for common fast-checks (smoke, safety, release-preflight); integrated metric exporters (prometheus pushgateway + internal eval-metrics uploader); added a PR annotation step to post a summarized table to the GitHub checks API; included unit tests and a small e2e runner that can be used in local dev. See docs/ci/eval-gate.md for usage and examples. Checklist: - [x] Add CI hook binary and CLI - [x] Add default fast profiles and thresholds - [x] Metric export + PR annotation - [x] Unit tests for metric comparators - [x] e2e smoke test for CI (uses small prompt-set) Notes and limitations: this gate is intentionally conservative and opt-in per repo via .github/workflows/eval_gate.yml. It currently supports numeric thresholds and a simple relative-delta rule; more advanced gating (per-prompt exceptions, contextual thresholds) will follow in subsequent PRs (ENG-3500). Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421/ci-eval-gating, example run: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/98765

notes: Gate is opt-in via .github/workflows/eval_gate.yml; recommended for model onboarding and release branches.
